subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and should that cache be limited to one reviewer instance with the full reviewed input as the key?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes when later requests bypass a fresh model review, so cache lifetime and key shape need explicit approval-boundary intent.

options.title: Approve exact-input per-instance memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the complete reviewed input, without persisting or converting them into durable approvals.

options.title: Memoize only low-risk allows
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower behavior change with fewer savings.

options.title: Keep fresh-review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model cost for now to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until maintainers want a cache boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-input per-instance memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the complete reviewed input, without persisting or converting them into durable approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent exec reviewer history make this the strongest available owner for the cache-boundary choice.
